newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi index falls despite active trading.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi index falls despite active trading.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index fell on Thursday on a drop in a number of blue chips but traded volume was high, brokers said.
The index fell 13.35 points to stand at 3057.83. Turnover gained to 20.314 million shillings on 661,345 shares compared to 8.661 million shillings on 228,172 shares on Wednesday.
He saw no significant reason for the index fall, saying that market fundamentals had not changed.

"There was good trading of shares at the general trading floor but strong activity was in Firestone East Africa which dealt a total of 414,900 shares that had been placed on the special board at 30.25 from 24.50," he said.
But elsewhere, British American Tobacco fell to 66 from 67.50, Bamburi Cement eased to 28.25 from 29 and Total Kenya fell to 71.50 from 72.

Brokers said a positive announcement that the World Bank had awarded institutions involved in the privatisation of Kenya Airways its 1996 award for excellence helped boost the stock, which remained steady at 10.10 on 47,167 shares.

Kenya Commercial Bank posted a post tax-profit of 1.29 billion shilling in the first six months of 1996 (January-June) compared to 823 million shillings. But that had no immediate impact on the stock, which was traded at 52, down from 52.50.
Nation Printers & Publishers rose a shilling to 106 while Standard Newspapers fell to 7.95 from 9.00. Barclays Bank shed a shilling to 103 and Diamond Trust fell to 37 fro 38.
